item.title: Tenryuji: Arashiyama's Great Zen Temple and Borrowed-Scenery Garden — Guide
item.description: Tenryuji is the most important temple in Arashiyama and one of Kyoto’s five great Zen temples, founded in 1339. While its wooden halls have burned and been rebuilt many times, its garden survives from the fourteenth century essentially unchanged — a masterpiece by the monk-designer Muso Soseki. Centred on a pond, it uses the technique of shakkei, ‘borrowed scenery’, drawing the wooded slopes of the Arashiyama hills into the composition so that garden and mountain read as one.
